hints: Use $\sin \theta = 0.8$ to find $\cos \theta = \sqrt{1 - 0.8^2} = 0.6$, and calculate normal reaction: $R = 80g \times 0.6 = 480\text{ N}$.
Calculate friction $F = \mu R = 0.1(480) = 48\text{ N}$ and component of weight down the slope $80g \times 0.8 = 640\text{ N}$.
Find acceleration down AB from $640 - 48 = 80a \implies a = 7.4\text{ m s}^{-2}$, then evaluate $v^2 = 2as = 2(7.4)(5)$.
walkthrough:
Step 1: Determine the normal reaction force on section AB.
Given $\sin \theta = 0.8$, by the Pythagorean identity:
$$\cos \theta = \sqrt{1 - \sin^2 \theta} = \sqrt{1 - 0.64} = \sqrt{0.36} = 0.6$$
Resolving perpendicular to section AB:
$$R = mg \cos \theta = 80 \times 10 \times 0.6 = 480\text{ N}$$

Step 2: Calculate the friction force opposing downward motion:
$$F = \mu R = 0.1 \times 480 = 48\text{ N}$$

Step 3: Component of weight down section AB:
$$W_{\parallel} = mg \sin \theta = 80 \times 10 \times 0.8 = 640\text{ N}$$

Step 4: Equation of motion along section AB:
$$W_{\parallel} - F = ma$$
$$640 - 48 = 80a$$
$$592 = 80a$$
$$a = \frac{592}{80} = 7.4\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Step 5: Calculate speed at B using suvat formula:
The man starts from rest at A ($u = 0$) and travels $s = 5\text{ m}$:
$$v^2 = u^2 + 2as$$
$$v^2 = 0^2 + 2(7.4)(5) = 74$$
$$v = \sqrt{74} \approx 8.6023\text{ m s}^{-1} \approx 8.60\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

hints: Calculate the loss of gravitational potential energy between B and C: $\Delta PE = mgh = 80(10)(2.5)$.
Calculate the gain in kinetic energy: $\Delta KE = \frac{1}{2}(80)(11^2 - 74)$.
Apply the work-energy equation: $\Delta PE - W_{\text{res}} = \Delta KE$ to find the work done against resistance.
walkthrough: Apply the work-energy principle between points B and C on the waterslide.

Step 1: Calculate the change in gravitational potential energy.
Point B is $2.5\text{ m}$ above the level of C, so the man descends a vertical height $h = 2.5\text{ m}$:
$$\Delta PE_{\text{lost}} = mgh = 80 \times 10 \times 2.5 = 2000\text{ J}$$

Step 2: Calculate the change in kinetic energy.
The speed at B is $v_B = \sqrt{74}\text{ m s}^{-1}$ ($v_B^2 = 74$), and the speed at C is $v_C = 11\text{ m s}^{-1}$ ($v_C^2 = 121$):
$$\Delta KE = \frac{1}{2}m(v_C^2 - v_B^2) = \frac{1}{2}(80)(121 - 74) = 40 \times 47 = 1880\text{ J}$$

Step 3: Apply the work-energy equation:
$$\text{Loss in PE} - \text{Work done against resistance} = \text{Gain in KE}$$
$$2000 - W = 1880$$
$$W = 2000 - 1880 = 120\text{ J}$$
